react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by tryptophan catabolism. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 5.6×10⁻¹⁸), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 1.59×10⁻⁸), and Mummichog m/z-direct networking (p = 0.00202) — KEGG:map00380 / hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' ranks as the unambiguous cross-paradigm winner. Seven of the ten input metabolites are direct members of this pathway: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and quinolinic acid. The consistent involvement of 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid across RaMP (fold enrichment 1044), Mummichog, and MetaboAnalystR strongly implicates the kynurenine/QUIN branch feeding NAD+ biosynthesis. The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 1.4×10⁻⁸, fold enrichment 1638) captures the upstream indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase–mediated oxidation of tryptophan, linking the three driver inputs (L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid) to inflammatory and neuroactive outcomes. Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.4×10⁻⁸) anchors the parallel neuroactive arm. L-Valine maps to Valine–leucine–isoleucine biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290, p = 0.044) but with only one overlapping metabolite, making it a minor independent signal. The biological picture is one of concerted tryptophan diversion: the treatment group shows coordinated elevation across both the neuroactive (serotonin–melatonin) and neurotoxic (quinolinic acid, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid) branches of tryptophan catabolism.
